## Bayesian R² for the full-training models

This is a posterior summary of training-model fit, reported with a 95% credible interval \[5\]. It is distinct from the predictive CV R² above and should be labelled separately.

```{r}
#| label: bayesian-r2
#| results: asis

bayesian_r2 <- list()
if (isTRUE(params$compute_bayesian_r2) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  for (dev in devices) {
    path <- file.path("models", "bayes_shared", "quadratic", paste0(dev, "_final_fit.rds"))
    if (file.exists(path)) {
      fit <- readRDS(path)
      r2 <- brms::bayes_R2(fit, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
      bayesian_r2[[dev]] <- data.frame(device = dev, evaluation = "Full-training Bayesian R2",
        estimate = r2[1, 1], posterior_sd = r2[1, 2], lower95 = r2[1, 3], upper95 = r2[1, 4])
    }
  }
}
if (length(bayesian_r2)) {
  bayesian_r2 <- do.call(rbind, bayesian_r2)
  print(show_table(bayesian_r2))
  write.csv(bayesian_r2, file.path(report_out, "bayesian_R2_training.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("Bayesian R2 below is a rounded summary from the supplied rendered HTML. Local saved fits take precedence when enabled.\n\n")
  print(show_table(snapshot_bayesian_r2))
}
```

# Common test comparison: R² and RMSE

The primary comparison is **Bayesian quadratic versus the RFE-selected random forest**, separately for FLIR and ICI. The all-feature RF and the two baselines are reference models. Both primary models use the same train/test subject assignments, response, predictor definitions and test individuals. Their model-specific transformations are fitted using training data only.

Test scoring is enabled in this integrated version because the task is now to compare the fixed approaches. The code checks shared training IDs, test IDs, outcomes and model input hashes. It uses saved Bayesian fits and either saved RF fits or validated RF prediction exports. All metrics below are from the same test observations; no CV or full-training R² is substituted into the comparison.

```{r}
#| label: evaluate-common-test
#| results: asis

if (isTRUE(params$evaluate_test)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install brms to read the fitted models.")
  test_out <- file.path("results", "combined_comparison")
  dir.create(test_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  split_path <- file.path("data", "bayes_shared", "supplied_subject_split.csv")
  plan <- read.csv(split_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(plan$SubjectID))
  test_scores <- test_intervals <- test_predictions <- list()
  test_inputs <- split_path

  apply_saved_preprocessing <- function(raw, bundle) {
    d <- raw[, c("target", bundle$features), drop = FALSE]
    parameters <- bundle$preprocessing
    for (v in bundle$features) {
      p <- parameters[parameters$variable == v, , drop = FALSE]
      stopifnot(nrow(p) == 1L, is.finite(p$median), is.finite(p$center), p$scale > 0)
      d[[v]][is.na(d[[v]])] <- p$median
      d[[v]] <- (d[[v]] - p$center) / p$scale
    }
    if (isTRUE(bundle$add_quadratic)) {
      p <- parameters[parameters$variable == "canthiMax_sq", , drop = FALSE]
      stopifnot(nrow(p) == 1L, is.finite(p$center), p$scale > 0)
      d$canthiMax_sq <- (d$canthiMax^2 - p$center) / p$scale
    }
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(d))))
    d
  }

  for (device_index in seq_along(devices)) {
    dev <- devices[device_index]
    bundle_path <- file.path("models", "bayes_shared", "quadratic", paste0(dev, "_final_bundle.rds"))
    train_path <- file.path("data", "bayes_shared", paste0(dev, "_train_unimputed.csv"))
    test_path <- file.path("data", "bayes_shared", paste0(dev, "_test_unimputed.csv"))
    bundle <- readRDS(bundle_path)
    train_raw <- read.csv(train_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    test_raw <- read.csv(test_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    stopifnot(isTRUE(bundle$diagnostics_passed), identical(bundle$device, dev),
              identical(bundle$model_name, "quadratic"), isTRUE(bundle$add_quadratic),
              !anyDuplicated(train_raw$SubjectID), !anyDuplicated(test_raw$SubjectID),
              all(train_raw$split == "train"), all(test_raw$split == "test"),
              setequal(train_raw$SubjectID, bundle$training_subject_ids),
              !length(intersect(bundle$training_subject_ids, test_raw$SubjectID)),
              !anyNA(match(test_raw$SubjectID, plan$SubjectID)),
              all(plan$split[match(test_raw$SubjectID, plan$SubjectID)] == "test"))
    fitted_hashes <- read.csv(file.path(base_results, "quadratic", "fitting_input_checksums.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    current_hash <- unname(tools::md5sum(train_path))
    index <- match(train_path, fitted_hashes$file)
    stopifnot(!is.na(index), identical(tolower(current_hash), tolower(fitted_hashes$checksum[index])))
    train <- apply_saved_preprocessing(train_raw, bundle)
    test <- apply_saved_preprocessing(test_raw, bundle)
    fit <- bundle$fit
    predicted <- colMeans(brms::posterior_epred(fit, newdata = test))
    set.seed(20261018L + 1000L + device_index)
    yrep <- brms::posterior_predict(fit, newdata = test, ndraws = 2000)
    bounds <- apply(yrep, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
    simple <- lm(target ~ canthiMax, data = train)
    d <- data.frame(device = dev, SubjectID = test_raw$SubjectID, Date = test_raw$Date,
      observed = test$target, mean_baseline = mean(train$target),
      simple_linear = as.numeric(predict(simple, newdata = test)),
      predicted = predicted, lower90 = bounds[1, ], upper90 = bounds[2, ])
    # Add RF predictions for exactly the same subjects and predictor definitions.
    rf_bundle_path <- file.path("models", "rf_shared", paste0(dev, "_final_bundle.rds"))
    rf_predictions_path <- file.path("results", "rf_shared", paste0(dev, "_test_predictions.csv"))
    rf_ids_path <- file.path("results", "rf_shared", paste0(dev, "_training_ids.csv"))
    if (file.exists(rf_bundle_path) && requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
      rf <- readRDS(rf_bundle_path)
      stopifnot(identical(rf$device, dev), identical(rf$protocol, "peer-rf-shared-split-v1"),
        identical(rf$features, bundle$features),
        setequal(rf$training_subject_ids, bundle$training_subject_ids),
        identical(tolower(rf$training_file_checksum), tolower(unname(tools::md5sum(train_path)))),
        length(rf$features_selected) > 0L, all(rf$features_selected %in% rf$features))
      med <- rf$median_imputer[rf$features]
      expected_med <- vapply(train_raw[rf$features], median, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)
      stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(med), unname(expected_med), tolerance = 1e-8)))
      X_test <- test_raw[rf$features]
      for (v in rf$features) X_test[[v]][is.na(X_test[[v]])] <- med[[v]]
      stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(X_test))))
      d$RF_selected <- predict(rf$fit_selected, data = X_test[rf$features_selected])$predictions
      d$RF_all <- predict(rf$fit_all, data = X_test)$predictions
      d$RF_source <- rf$origin
      test_inputs <- c(test_inputs, rf_bundle_path)
    } else if (file.exists(rf_predictions_path) && file.exists(rf_ids_path)) {
      rf_predictions <- read.csv(rf_predictions_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      rf_ids <- read.csv(rf_ids_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      stopifnot(all(c("SubjectID", "observed", "RF_selected", "RF_all") %in% names(rf_predictions)),
        !anyDuplicated(rf_predictions$SubjectID), !anyDuplicated(rf_ids$SubjectID),
        setequal(rf_predictions$SubjectID, d$SubjectID),
        setequal(rf_ids$SubjectID, bundle$training_subject_ids))
      rf_predictions <- rf_predictions[match(d$SubjectID, rf_predictions$SubjectID), ]
      stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(rf_predictions$observed, d$observed, tolerance = 1e-8)))
      if ("device" %in% names(rf_predictions)) stopifnot(all(rf_predictions$device == dev))
      d$RF_selected <- rf_predictions$RF_selected
      d$RF_all <- rf_predictions$RF_all
      d$RF_source <- "Validated exported RF test predictions with shared training IDs"
      test_inputs <- c(test_inputs, rf_predictions_path, rf_ids_path)
    } else if (file.exists(rf_bundle_path)) {
      stop("Install ranger to predict with the saved RF models, or provide the validated RF prediction CSV exports.")
    } else {
      stop("Missing RF fits/predictions for ", dev, ". Enable fit_rf, or export the collaborator's existing res object first.")
    }
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(d$RF_selected)), all(is.finite(d$RF_all)))

    score_labels <- c(mean_baseline = "Training mean", simple_linear = "Simple linear",
      predicted = "Bayesian quadratic", RF_selected = "Random forest (selected)",
      RF_all = "Random forest (all predictors)")
    for (model in names(score_labels)) {
      test_scores[[length(test_scores) + 1L]] <- data.frame(device = dev,
        model = unname(score_labels[[model]]), evaluation = "Matched supplied test subjects", score_predictions(d$observed, d[[model]]))
    }
    test_intervals[[dev]] <- data.frame(device = dev, n = nrow(d),
      coverage90 = mean(d$observed >= d$lower90 & d$observed <= d$upper90),
      mean_width90 = mean(d$upper90 - d$lower90))
    test_predictions[[dev]] <- d
    write.csv(d, file.path(test_out, paste0(dev, "_test_predictions.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
    test_inputs <- c(test_inputs, bundle_path, train_path, test_path)
  }
  test_scores <- do.call(rbind, test_scores)
  test_intervals <- do.call(rbind, test_intervals)
  write.csv(test_scores, file.path(test_out, "test_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(test_intervals, file.path(test_out, "test_intervals.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  hashes <- tools::md5sum(test_inputs)
  write.csv(data.frame(file = names(hashes), algorithm = "MD5", checksum = unname(hashes)),
            file.path(test_out, "evaluation_input_checksums.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(c(
    "Fixed model: per-device Gaussian regression, 29 predictors plus standardized canthiMax square.",
    "Reference coefficient prior SD 0.5. Models are read from the saved quadratic final bundles.",
    "RF selected model is primary; all-feature RF is a reference. No winner is selected from test scores during training.",
    "RF training IDs must match the Bayesian training IDs; test IDs/outcomes are checked before metrics.",
    "RF medians come from outer training only. RF inner CV preprocessing follows the peer method.",
    "Saved training medians, centers and scales are applied unchanged to test predictors.",
    "Test IDs must be disjoint from saved training IDs and agree with the supplied split.",
    "Point prediction: mean posterior_epred; intervals: 5th and 95th posterior_predict percentiles.",
    "Predictive seed: 20261018 + 1000 + device_index; 2000 predictive draws.",
    "R2 = 1 - SSE/SST using the test outcome mean; errors and interval widths are in degrees Celsius.",
    "Report this as the supplied-split evaluation. Earlier pilot work used a different split.",
    "Do not revise the model repeatedly in response to these test results."
  ), file.path(test_out, "evaluation_record.txt"))
  print(show_table(test_scores))
  print(show_table(test_intervals))
    main_comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(devices, function(dev) {
      b <- test_scores[test_scores$device == dev & test_scores$model == "Bayesian quadratic", , drop = FALSE]
      r <- test_scores[test_scores$device == dev & test_scores$model == "Random forest (selected)", , drop = FALSE]
      stopifnot(nrow(b) == 1L, nrow(r) == 1L, b$n == r$n)
      difference <- b$RMSE - r$RMSE
      better <- if (abs(difference) < 1e-10) "Numerical tie" else
        if (difference < 0) "Bayesian quadratic" else "Random forest (selected)"
      data.frame(device = dev, n = b$n, Bayesian_R2 = b$R2, RF_R2 = r$R2,
        Bayesian_RMSE = b$RMSE, RF_RMSE = r$RMSE,
        RMSE_difference_Bayes_minus_RF = difference, lower_test_RMSE = better)
    }))
    write.csv(main_comparison, file.path(test_out, "main_model_comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    cat("\n\n### Primary model comparison\n\n")
    print(show_table(main_comparison))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(main_comparison))) {
      row <- main_comparison[i, ]
      if (row$lower_test_RMSE == "Numerical tie") {
        cat("\n\n", row$device, ": the primary models have numerically equal test RMSE.\n", sep = "")
      } else {
        cat("\n\n", row$device, ": **", row$lower_test_RMSE,
          "** has the lower observed test RMSE, by ",
          sprintf("%.4f", abs(row$RMSE_difference_Bayes_minus_RF)), " degrees Celsius.\n", sep = "")
      }
    }
    cat("\n\nThe comparison uses identical subjects and outcomes within each device. With the same R2 denominator, a lower RMSE also gives a higher R2. These are observed test-set differences; they do not establish a universal or statistically significant advantage.\n")


} else {
  cat("Final test scoring is deferred. This evaluation block has not read or scored test observations.\n")
}
```

For a given device and identical test outcomes, both models have the same R² denominator. The model with lower RMSE therefore also has higher predictive R². The two metrics describe the same squared-error comparison in different units. The comparison reports the observed difference rather than treating it as proof of a general or statistically significant advantage.

```{r}
#| label: fig-common-test-predictions

  paired <- do.call(rbind, test_predictions)
  plot_data <- rbind(
    data.frame(device = paired$device, model = "Bayesian quadratic", observed = paired$observed, predicted = paired$predicted),
    data.frame(device = paired$device, model = "Random forest (selected)", observed = paired$observed, predicted = paired$RF_selected))
  ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(observed, predicted)) +
```

```{r}
#| label: common-temperature-strata

if (isTRUE(params$evaluate_test) && exists("test_predictions")) {
  strata_scores <- list()
  for (dev in devices) {
    d <- test_predictions[[dev]]
    strata <- ifelse(d$observed >= 37.5, ">=37.5 degrees C", "<37.5 degrees C")
    for (level in unique(strata)) for (model in c("predicted", "RF_selected")) {
      group <- d[strata == level, ]
      strata_scores[[length(strata_scores) + 1L]] <- data.frame(device = dev,
        stratum = level, model = if (model == "predicted") "Bayesian quadratic" else "Random forest (selected)",
        n = nrow(group), RMSE = sqrt(mean((group$observed - group[[model]])^2)),
        MAE = mean(abs(group$observed - group[[model]])))
    }
  }
  strata_scores <- do.call(rbind, strata_scores)
  show_table(strata_scores)
} else cat("Temperature-stratum test errors have not been calculated in this render.\n")
```

The temperature strata provide descriptive error summaries. Small subgroup counts limit interpretation; this regression comparison does not itself establish a diagnostic screening threshold.

# Discussion and limitations

The final test comparison above determines which primary method has lower observed prediction error within each device. Its verdict is generated only from matched test predictions.

The shared-data results support the single quadratic extension as the Bayesian candidate. It improves aggregate CV errors for both devices, reduces the main residual curvature and preserves approximately nominal pooled interval coverage. Predictive performance is stable over the examined coefficient prior settings.

Several limitations remain. The central predictive density is flatter than the observed density. The lowest ICI predictions retain bias, and sparse temperature extremes limit assessment there. Correlated facial predictors complicate interpretation of individual coefficients. Available-round averaging gives variables and subjects different numbers of contributing measurements. The shared cleaning cutoff may also restrict the range of facial temperatures represented.

The supplied outer split separates subjects, while the inner CV separates acquisition dates. Test subjects may still share collection dates with training subjects. This study does not establish performance in a different clinical setting, with new device calibration or in a population with a different temperature distribution.

The RF tuning and RFE scores are development results; their resampling and preprocessing differ from the Bayesian CV. The final comparison uses a separate common subject test split. The same Bayesian CV results were inspected during model development. Earlier pilot work used round-one measurements and a different split; its results are excluded from the main comparison here. The project should retain that history and describe final evaluation using the supplied assignments without claiming an entirely untouched historical holdout unless the earlier subject usage has been checked.

# FAIR and reproducibility

FAIR concerns whether research objects can be found, accessed, connected and reused \[7\]. CV and sampling diagnostics assess statistical reliability; code, metadata, provenance, identifiers and licensing support FAIR reuse.

| Principle | Included in this workflow | Release action |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Findable | Dataset DOI/version, descriptive title, author, metadata and named outputs. | Add the project repository URL and an archived release identifier. |
| Accessible | Public source link, readable HTML and executable source. | Keep the report, metadata and access instructions available. |
| Interoperable | CSV tables, `SubjectID` keys, explicit variable names, ISO dates and units. | Retain the variable dictionary and link derived files to their inputs. |
| Reusable | CC0 source data, MIT code, cleaning logs, priors, seeds, folds and checksums. | Commit the actual `renv.lock`, release version and contributor information. |

The preparation step exports `variable_dictionary.csv`, correction logs and raw input checksums. The fit scripts retain fold assignments, preprocessing parameters, posterior summaries and environment records. This report exports the metrics it displays and machine-readable analysis metadata. A source DOI alone does not give the project code its own persistent identifier.

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility-record

metadata <- data.frame(
  field = c("analysis_version", "author", "dataset_doi", "dataset_version", "data_license", "code_license",
    "target", "target_unit", "base_predictors", "quadratic_predictor", "coefficient_prior_sd",
    "outer_split", "cv_scheme", "cv_seed", "test_evaluation_enabled", "repository_url", "archive_doi"),
  value = c("0.2.0", "Lei Huang and project collaborator", "10.13026/3bhc-9065", "1.0.0", "CC0-1.0", "MIT",
    "aveOralM", "degrees Celsius", "29", "standardized square of standardized canthiMax", "0.5",
    "data/split_train_test_aveOralM.csv", "five-fold acquisition-date groups", "20261018",
    as.character(isTRUE(params$evaluate_test)), params$repository_url, params$archive_doi))

  field = c("primary_rf", "rf_rfe_resamples", "rf_inner_imputation", "primary_comparison"),
  value = c("RFE-selected and training-CV tuned ranger forest", "3 x 5 date groups",
    "outer-training medians before inner resampling; peer method preserved",
    "Bayesian quadratic versus RF selected on identical supplied test subjects")))
write.csv(metadata, file.path(report_out, "analysis_metadata.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(cv_metrics[, c("device", "model", "source")], file.path(report_out, "result_provenance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(report_out, "render_sessionInfo.txt"))

if (file.exists(qmd)) {
  hash <- tools::md5sum(qmd)
  write.csv(data.frame(file = names(hash), algorithm = "MD5", checksum = unname(hash)),
            file.path(report_out, "report_source_checksum.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
show_table(data.frame(
  item = c("renv.lock", "Repository URL", "Archived release identifier"),
  status = c(if (file.exists("renv.lock")) "Present; verify it matches the successful analysis environment" else "Not present in this project copy",
    if (nzchar(params$repository_url)) params$repository_url else "Not supplied",
    if (nzchar(params$archive_doi)) params$archive_doi else "Not supplied")))
```

# Appendix: Full-training coefficient summaries

The following tables load the saved 95% coefficient summaries when available. They come from one full-training fit per device. Fold-specific posteriors are not pooled into a single posterior. Because the facial variables are correlated, coefficient intervals should be interpreted as conditional associations within the specified model.

```{r}
#| label: coefficient-summaries
#| results: asis

for (dev in devices) {
  path <- file.path(base_results, "quadratic", paste0(dev, "_coefficients_95.csv"))
  cat("\n\n### ", dev, "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    coefficients <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
    cat(as.character(show_table(coefficients)), sep = "\n")
  } else {
    snapshot_path <- file.path("report_assets", "quadratic", paste0(dev, "_coefficients_95_reported.csv"))
    if (file.exists(snapshot_path)) {
      cat("Rounded coefficient summary from the supplied rendered HTML:\n\n")
      cat(as.character(show_table(read.csv(snapshot_path, check.names = FALSE))), sep = "\n")
    } else cat("Saved coefficient summaries are not available in this copy.\n")
  }
}
```
